overview.oneLineTake: A sharp rebound into unresolved Nvidia and liquidity risks leaves the tape two-sided, so respect wide swings and keep short-premium sizing modest.
themes: Equities rebounded hard Monday: QQQ closed 679.35 (+3.54%) and SPY 752.69 (+2.37%), though commentary still argues over whether the AI trade has cracked.
Nvidia is the headline risk: reports of a widening spy scandal and scrutiny of CEO Jensen Huang keep AI leadership in question while Anthropic's reported IPO roadshow adds supply.
Liquidity is a worry: pieces on tightening liquidity and a "Quant Quake II" selloff point to positioning-driven moves rather than clean trends.
Oil fell on reports that IAEA inspectors may return to Iran and that Iran eased Hormuz demands. Both are unconfirmed.
Growth data stays firm: jobless claims near historic lows and GDP nowcasts signal a strong finish to 2026. The 10-year yield was 4.86% as of Nov 6.
risks: Nvidia investigation fallout hitting megacap AI names.
Quant and liquidity-driven air pockets after a +3% QQQ day.
Geopolitical headline reversal on Iran and Hormuz sending oil back up.

intelligence.headline: Jensen Huang Puts $200 Billion Dent in Nvidia's Stock Price
intelligence.summary: Nvidia is down about 4.5% in premarket trading, a roughly $200 billion hit at the open, after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair with suspected Chinese spy Huang Le of Singapore-based Megaspeed, raising questions about whether he remains at the company that peaked at $5.8 trillion about a month ago and now stands at $4.5 trillion, second only to Apple, with no immediate direct impact on sales and earnings.

intelligence.headline: On the Move: Berkshire, Greenfire, Sanofi
intelligence.summary: Berkshire Hathaway edged up 0.3% in premarket trading after spending about $9.6 billion buying back shares in the third quarter even as operating earnings fell; US-listed Greenfire Resources jumped 36% after Strathcona Resources agreed to buy the company; Sanofi rose 1.9% in Paris after BNP Paribas upgraded the shares to outperform, citing Dupixent; KKR, Constellation Energy and Barrick Mining report before the open, with Take-Two, Occidental Petroleum, Rocket Lab, Skydance and Hims & Hers Health after the close.

intelligence.headline: US Inflation Set to Simmer Down Some After Recent Pickup
intelligence.summary: Tuesday's October CPI, the last before the Federal Reserve's December meeting when policymakers are expected to boost interest rates, is likely to show prices for US goods and services rose at a slower pace after two uncomfortable months; investors will also watch earnings from CoreWeave and Cisco Systems and the potential kickoff of Anthropic's marketing effort for its IPO.

intelligence.headline: Why Many Americans' Budgets Feel Stretched in a Strong Economy
intelligence.summary: A rising stock market and a growing economy are no consolation to many Americans who have been squeezed by years of rising costs.
